newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan stocks end higher, forecasts divided.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan stocks end higher, forecasts divided.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed higher on buying by local investors, particulaly retail investors, on Tuesday but analysts were divided over the future trend.
The all share index closed 4.59 points higher at 585.29, continuing a slow upward movement. The index has risen by more than four percent in the past two weeks.
"The rise is retail-driven. I doubt it can be sustained because there has not been a fundamental change on the ground," said Gihan Rajapakse of CTC Eagle Fund Management.
But some brokers said recent buying was based on the belief corporate performance would improve in the second half of 1996.
Corporate results in the first half of this year were dismal following a crippling drought which resulted in extensive power cuts, badly hitting the manufacturing industry.
Gainers led decliners by 41 to eight. Central Finance rose 3.75 rupees to 244.75 and Hayleys 12 rupees to 205.
Turnover was a moderate 15 million rupees. Foreign purchases were limited to 2.3 million rupees and sales were one million.
"There is foreign buying interest among selected blue chips at market prices. But they are not willing to chase stocks," a broker with a foreign joint venture broking firm said.
